features.text: The patient is 100 years old and female.
The patient experiences shortness of breath when walking too fast or drinking a whole glass of water without stopping.
The patient experiences dizziness, which is managed with a pill not taken every day.
The patient feels overly tired due to the medications she takes.
The patient has swelling in her ankles that has been present for about six months and comes and goes.
The patient does not have chest pain.
The patient does not have palpitations.
The patient takes amlodipine and lisinopril for blood pressure, simvastatin for lipids, and levothyroxine for hyperthyroidism.
The patient takes a pill for dizziness when it occurs, but not every day.
The patient has a family history of heart problems, including a heart attack in her son, a stroke in her brother, and a heart issue in her eldest sister.
The patient has had several surgeries over the years but is unsure of the exact ones.
The patient does not smoke and has no allergies to medications.
The patient was told by her doctor that she has a new worrisome heart murmur, but was not given details about its timing, characteristics, or changes over time.
The patient was told by her doctor that she had a chest x-ray last week but was not given the results or any details about them.
The patient has not been following up with a cardiologist specifically.
The patient has not been informed if she has had an echocardiogram or ECG in the past six months.
The patient has not been informed of the results of the chest x-ray performed last week.
The patient has not been informed if the heart murmur has changed in intensity or characteristics over time.
The patient has not been informed if the heart murmur changes with activity or position.
The patient has not been informed of the timing (systolic or diastolic) or specific qualities (e.g., rumbling, blowing, harsh) of the heart murmur.
The patient has not been informed of the exact timing of when the heart murmur was first detected.
